name: cnsplots-v3
summary: Publication-ready scientific visualization in Python across major journals (Cell default, Nature, Science). Features an actionable 6-step closed-loop workflow (environment -> data profiling & plot mapping -> layout architecture & budgeting -> ~100 pt build with no font or marker blow-ups -> statistical truth extraction & cleanup -> output verification), dual execution modes (cnsplots native or pure matplotlib/seaborn via standalone cns_cell.mplstyle; seaborn optional), 360 dpi display/export, explicit pt units, and a dedicated references/plot-catalog.md.

changes: Restructured SKILL.md into a deterministic, data-driven 6-step closed-loop workflow (SOP).
Decoupled the 30+ plot function catalog into a standalone references/plot-catalog.md.
Exported standalone styles/cns_cell.mplstyle for zero-dependency fallback via pure matplotlib/seaborn.
Added proactive environment branching: prompt user to choose between installing cnsplots or using pure mplstyle.
Enforced a ~100 pt (80, 100, 120, 150) panel sizing baseline and banned font or marker blow-ups; Mode B sets marker and patch geometry in the style sheet.
Set the Cell Press 10-color palette as the skill's house style (the cnsplots package default remains Ecotyper1), with support for Nature, Science, and other journal styles.
Set an Arial-first font stack with Nimbus Sans / Liberation Sans Linux fallbacks across templates and workflows.
Encapsulated default house style configurations (Cell palette, viridis, Arial-first fonts, pdf/svg fonttype, 360 dpi display/export, opaque background) into reusable apply_house_style() functions.
Enforced copying cns_cell.mplstyle into project directories for isolated, reproducible pure matplotlib/seaborn execution.
Generated cns_cell.mplstyle and cell_colors.py from cns.palettes('Cell') and added a --check drift test in export_mplstyle.py.
Standardized final delivery on PDF (SVG for editing, PNG preview only) and visual inspection instead of file-existence scripts.
Made units explicit: cns.figure(..., unit='pt'), multipanel(..., unit='pt'), and renamed the sizing reference to panel-sizing-100pt.md.
Unified display, preview, and export dpi at 360.
Vendored the cnsplots Figure 1 and Figure 2 showcases under templates/upstream-showcase/ with pt units, 360 export dpi, and the upstream 144 display dpi needed for their pixel-tuned layout.
Documented matplotlib 3.10 vs 3.11 figsize units; 3.11+ examples use the explicit (width, height, unit) form.
Showcase scripts emit PDF and SVG next to the scripts by default.
